title: Women, brewery sponsors and the perks of being a DJ
summary: The DJs enjoyed attention from women and hospitality from brewing companies, 1950-62.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: But you met a lot of women, huh, Tex?

Oh, boy. It was a lot of fun. It was a lot of fun. We enjoyed ourselves. Oh, wow. Because you know, you didn't want to go crazy or nothing like that, because they had women everywhere, and they just wanted to take you home to dinner. And some women did, and some women took us out to cocktails at the various clubs. In fact, I hardly had to spend any money because, you know, then you had companies and advertisers who felt proud to, like the Falstead Brewing Company and the Blatt's Brewing Company and the Jack's Brewing Company. They all wanted to do something for us, you know. They wanted to come down to the club and invite the people, or come down to the plant and let the people see how we operate. There's so much that happened from 1950 until 1962 until I just couldn't put it, you wouldn't have enough tapes for me to put it on. It's just something that went on.
